subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Which owner boundary should drive the next step for this multi-agent Telegram/provider timeout report: require a live current-main reproduction first, promote a narrower runtime/channel bottleneck fix, or accept the merged fallback mitigations as sufficient only after proof?
rationale: The report crosses Telegram runner concurrency, model fallback, provider transport, runtime scheduling, session locks, launch defaults, and operator configuration; current source shows partial mitigations but not enough evidence to choose a safe implementation boundary automatically.

options.title: Run canonical live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram trace with provider, fallback, lane, and polling diagnostics before choosing code changes.

options.title: Promote a narrower bottleneck fix
options.body: If maintainers already know the failing layer, open or designate a focused issue for that boundary and link this report as supporting evidence.

options.title: Close after mitigation proof
options.body: Treat merged fallback work as sufficient only if a current-main run shows the original simultaneous timeout pattern no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Run canonical live repro first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram trace with provider, fallback, lane, and polling diagnostics before choosing code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner is the best available routing candidate because the remaining decision spans fallback, provider timeout, Telegram concurrency, and docs surfaces with history in that area.
